objective: The rung-C culmination: a downstream worker (opencode) executes a delegated edge-screener task in a LOOP governed by the contract — implement → score against the contract's deterministic guardrails → feed the failing guardrail back → retry → until pass or an iteration budget. Measure whether the loop (a) RECOVERS the single-shot floors Phase 101 found (decision-lag: the worker couldn't implement the subtle pending-lag in one shot even when told the invariant) and (b) produces TRUTHFUL work vs GAMING the guardrails over iterations (passes the loop but fails a HELD-OUT validation it never sees). Connects all three pillars: the check (1) + the dashboard (3) + the loop (2).
recommendation: Recommend a contract-driven loop where the worker iterates against the contract's VISIBLE guardrails (NOT the held-out integrity test), with RICH feedback (the failing guardrail's assertion error / counterexample — not just pass/fail), and a SEPARATE held-out validation run at the end to detect gaming. Arms: single-shot (Ph101 baseline) vs contract-loop vs bare-loop (loop on functional tests only, no named invariant) — to isolate the loop's value from the contract's. Focus on decision-lag (the floor) + ≥1 other in-band task. The crux is feedback richness: pass/fail alone likely won't recover the subtle floor; the assertion error / counterexample likely will.

options.label: A — Contract-loop with rich feedback + held-out gaming validation
options.description: Worker iterates against the contract's VISIBLE guardrails with rich feedback (failing assertion + counterexample); a held-out integrity test validates the converged impl (gaming = loop-pass but held-out-fail). Arms: single-shot vs contract-loop vs bare-loop. Measures floor-recovery, iterations-to-converge, gaming rate. Reuses Ph100/101 infra.

options.label: B — Pass/fail loop only (minimal)
options.description: The loop feeds back only pass/fail of the contract check; no rich feedback. Simpler, but likely floors on decision-lag too (the worker can't tell WHY it failed) — risks an uninformative null that conflates 'loops don't help' with 'this feedback is too thin'.

options.label: C — General downstream-worker execution (no loop focus)
options.description: Build broader pillar-2 plumbing (Agent/Workflow worker orchestration) without the contract-loop experiment. Defers the agent-loop question; less directly tied to the Ph100/101 findings.

assumptions.text: FEEDBACK RICHNESS is the experimental variable, not loop-presence: the loop feeds back the failing guardrail's assertion error / counterexample (rich), because pass/fail alone likely won't recover the subtle decision-lag floor (single-shot WITH the invariant named already floored — the worker needs to know WHY/where it broke). Possibly a feedback-richness arm.

The loop iterates against the contract's VISIBLE guardrails (not the held-out integrity test), with a SEPARATE held-out validation run at the end — else the worker iterates-to-green ON the held-out test (the Ph101 ceiling confound, now by design). Gaming = passes the visible-guardrail loop but fails the held-out validation. This split makes the loop meaningful AND detects gaming.

Arms = single-shot (Ph101 baseline) vs contract-loop vs bare-loop (loop on functional tests only, no named invariant) — to isolate the LOOP's value from the contract's invariant. Corpus focuses on decision-lag (the floor) + ≥1 other in-band task. Measures: floor-recovery rate, iterations-to-converge, gaming rate.

Worker substrate = opencode loop (opencode run --continue/--session for iteration, accumulating context — proven in Ph100/101) vs a Claude Agent/Workflow loop (Jake earlier leaned reuse-Agent/Workflow before any opencode fleet, but opencode is now the proven worker). Capped iterations (~5), smaller corpus, controls-first + byte-frozen pre-registration.

context.active_phase: Phase 101 — Harder-corpus contract screen DELIVERED (contract helps task-specifically; decision-lag FLOORED single-shot). Phase 102 = pillar 2, the contract-driven loop.
open_decisions: The crux (A1): can a contract-driven loop recover the single-shot floor? Hinges on feedback richness, not the loop per se.
Reuses check-fidelity.py + the opencode runner + the frozen edge-screener corpus (esp. decision-lag).
Gaming detection (A2): the held-out validation catches a worker that iterates-to-green on the visible guardrails but isn't genuinely correct.
